PodDeleteMode.description:
How pod-delete removes pods (maps to the vetted experiment's FORCE env).

GRACEFUL: default Kubernetes deletion; the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds
          applies (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace period).
FORCE:    deletion with gracePeriodSeconds=0; containers are killed at once.

get.description: Counts, score/recovery statistics and recent runs from persisted experiments.

Always 200; each check says whether that dependency answered.

Probes are read-only (list workloads, Prometheus build info) and bounded by the
configured request timeouts.

post.description: Stop an active experiment: its own ChaosEngine only, then ABORTED.

Capture a steady-state baseline from Prometheus.

Success moves BASELINING -> INJECTING; a failed capture is recorded and the
experiment stays in BASELINING so it can be retried. No fault is injected.

Start the pod-delete fault via LitmusChaos (INJECTING experiments only).

Blocks until the target pods are confirmed deleted (-> OBSERVING) or the start
fails/times out (-> INJECTION_FAILED, ChaosEngine stopped).

Advance observation by one bounded step (call repeatedly while in progress).

OBSERVING -> RECOVERING once Litmus finishes; RECOVERING -> COMPLETED when the
recovery rule holds; -> UNKNOWN (with reason and cause) when it cannot be
established. Read-only except stopping our own ChaosEngine on a Litmus timeout.

Start the automatic lifecycle (idempotent).

Accepts a CREATED experiment, or one that passed POST /validate and has not
started (BASELINING without a baseline). The orchestrator then drives it to
COMPLETED/UNKNOWN and cleans up; follow it with GET /experiments/{id}.

get.description:
The persisted Resilience Score (or the reason it was not scored).

`?version=v1` recomputes that methodology from the same stored evidence
(deterministic; not persisted). 404 until the experiment has finished.

post.description:
Run static then cluster safety checks.

The outcome is the resulting state (BASELINING / VALIDATION_FAILED), not the HTTP status.
Save a reviewed import (PLANNED). Nothing is deployed.

get.description: What can be imported, and whether deployment is available here.

post.description: Parse, validate and plan; stores nothing and contacts no cluster.

delete.description: Forget a removed (or never deployed) import's record.

post.description: Apply the reviewed plan (explicit approval: its digest and confirm=true).
One read-only health check; moves DEPLOYING on, and REMOVING to REMOVED.
Delete the import's namespace after verifying it owns it (typed confirmation).

get.description:
200 when the database is reachable and migrated to this API's head, else 503.

`/health` only says the process is up; use this to know whether normal
operations (experiments, history, services) can work.

Deployments and StatefulSets outside system namespaces, with experiment history.

Replica counts are the controllers' own status (as `kubectl get` shows them).

Live pod health plus this workload's experiments, scores and tested faults.

If the cluster cannot be queried, history is still returned with
health UNKNOWN and the error in `cluster_error`.

Nodes and edges read from the cluster now (see docs/topology.md).

Without `namespace`: every namespace the cluster's access allows.
